graphics.alt_text: Example 1: Lake Huron. Top-left: posterior mean estimates and 95 percent CrIs of the estimated quantiles, plotted with the data (grey). Top-right: forecasted quantile estimates and 95 percent credible intervals (seen after 1972), along with the filtered quantile estimates and 95 percent credible intervals (seen from 1952 to 1972). Bottom-left: synthesized posterior predictive 95 percent interval over the observed period. Bottom-right: observed-period synthesis near the forecast origin (lighter band) and synthesized posterior predictive 95 percent interval over the eight-step forecast window (slightly darker rose band); the vertical dotted line marks the forecast origin.

Example 2: Sunspots. Top: The sunspot time series from 1700 to 1988. Bottom left: posterior mean estimates and 95 percent CrIs of the estimated quantiles from the DQLM (red) and exDQLM (blue), plotted with the data (grey) from 1780 to 1830. Bottom right: Histogram of samples from the approximated posterior distribution of under the exDQLM.

Example 2: Sunspots. The QQ plots (left column), ACF plots of the PIT sequence (center column), and MAP one-step-ahead standardized forecast errors (right column) from the DQLM (red) and exDQLM (blue).

Example 4: sparse static exAL regression under the correlated Gaussian benchmark with the rhs ns prior. Black diamonds denote the true non-intercept coefficients, orange intervals denote LDVB 95 percent posterior intervals, and blue intervals denote MCMC 95 percent posterior intervals. Panels correspond to p_0 = 0.05, 0.25, and 0.50 .

Observed USGS daily water flow on the (1 + x) scale, with x measured in m^3/s, May 29, 1987 through December 25, 2022. Horizontal dashed lines show approximate current-rating discharge equivalents of the current NWS minor and major stage categories at BTEC1/USGS 11160500, computed from USGS stage-discharge rating 40.0 and transformed to the plotting scale env-cnrfc_btec1,env-usgs_11160500_rating40. They are operational magnitude references for the discharge scale, not historical flood-stage classifications of daily-mean observations.

Synthesized exAL-M-T1 prediction at December 25, 2022, on the (1+x) scale, with x in m^3/s. The 19 historical and 28 forecast dates show historical observations and held-out verification values. The origin is T and the first lead is T+1. The maroon line is the predictive mean, the pink band is the pointwise central 95 percent predictive interval, and ten gray traces connect predictive sample values within each period. GloFAS and NWS/NWM products give source context. Horizontal guides mark approximately 182 and 429 m^3/s.

Quantile reliability over eight and 28 days, pooling 40 and 140 cases across five origins. Curves give frequencies at or below predictive quantiles for exAL-M-T1, raw GloFAS/NWS, EMOS-GLOFAS, and seasonal climatology; the diagonal denotes nominal probabilities. NWS is available over eight days.

Two stacked panels use the same date range and vertical scale. The first shows historical USGS observations, retrospective GloFAS, 51 issued ensemble paths and held-out USGS observations. The second shows seven Q--DESN (AL) quantile curves over the same 30 historical and 28 forecast dates. A vertical line marks the forecast origin in both panels.

Three density panels show the same strongly left-skewed standardized population at content c=0.80. The green equal-tailed interval is [-1.00, 0.71], the blue mean-preserving interval is [-2.29, 0.64], and the orange shortest-contiguous interval is [-0.39, 0.84]. The MPI extends farthest into the left tail, whereas the shortest-contiguous interval is the narrowest and lies farthest to the right. These are population functionals rather than finite-sample comparisons.

Population recovery tilts across symmetric and skewed distributions. Every interval has content c=0.80 . Targets are computed on each raw population law and then displayed after mean/standard-deviation standardization. The top row shows standardized densities with equal-tailed (ET), MPI, and shortest-contiguous (SH) intervals; the bottom row shows the standardized width profile along the MTI family. In the Normal reference case the three targets coincide at / SD(Y)=0 . Under skewness, ET and SH generally require nonzero, distribution-specific recovery tilts, while MPI remains the zero-tilt retained-mean-balance target. The deterministic display is a population map for external target specification.

Four panels compare independent-sample content-attainment rates at n=50, 100, 500, and 1000 for the feasible target contents. Green, pink, and black vertical segments give the ranges across the eight simulation distributions for MTI, Young--Mathew, and Wilks, respectively. The vertical scale runs from 0.85 to 1.00, and a horizontal dashed line marks the nominal tolerance confidence 0.95. Wilks is at or near 1.00 in several cells; the MTI and Young--Mathew ranges lie closer to 0.95.

Nine panels compare interval widths for the feasible sample-size and target-content cells. Within each panel, rows correspond to the Gaussian, Student t(3), exponential, asymmetric-Laplace, two-piece-Normal, Beta, Gamma, and log-normal simulation laws. Green, pink, and black horizontal segments show empirical 2.5--97.5 percent width ranges for MTI, Young--Mathew, and Wilks; crosses mark their mean widths, and short dashed gray markers give the known population shortest-interval widths. The logarithmic horizontal scale retains raw interval lengths and shows that relative width varies substantially by distribution and design cell.

Four panels summarize the reported tensile metric for 187 batches and 1000 paired random splits. Panel A shows the empirical CDF and the MTI, Young--Mathew, and Wilks intervals from representative split 665; MTI is left-shifted and narrower than the two benchmarks in that split. Panels B and C plot held-out-content difference against width difference, each defined as MTI minus Young--Mathew or Wilks; most width differences are negative, and crosses mark the paired medians. Panel D shows lower-tail omission with open markers and upper-tail omission with filled markers, together with interquartile and empirical 95 percent ranges for each method.
Nine panels compare four models using mean forecast check loss and 95 percent intervals over 300 scored targets.

Eight panels compare oracle finite-grid average CRPS under asymmetric-Laplace tails, Gaussian-mixture, Laplace, nonlinear-reservoir, Gaussian, persistent-heavy-tail, regime-shift, and Student-t location--scale mechanisms. Each panel has four rows: MQ--DESN and independently fitted Q--DESN under AL and exAL. Points are posterior means and horizontal segments are equal-tailed 95 percent intervals for the score, with smaller values preferred. Filled symbols denote MQ--DESN and open symbols Q--DESN; blue circles denote AL and brown triangles exAL. Right-side annotations give raw adjacent-level crossing percentages before the specified monotone scoring transformation.
